summary: Pinnacle Knob station by 1916; the tower frame is gone and its foundation is now an overlook, though a 2024 account is unclear.

facts.status_note: Tower frame gone; only the foundation is described as remaining, and it is now an overlook.

staffing.status: watchman lived five miles from the station

access.note: Inside the Allegheny Wildlife Management Area. A visitor advises a four-wheel-drive vehicle for the steep last stretch of South Tower Lane.

events.note: Station on Pinnacle Knob in the state's 1916 report, with a watchman and a telephone line. The report does not give a build date.
Charleston Gazette item, quoted on the source page, refers to the Pinnacle Knob tower telephone.
Photo caption: a view from the rebuilt fire tower, taken in 1964. The rebuild date is not given.
Photo caption: only the frame of the fire tower was left, and a large communication tower stood on the summit.

evidence.supports: 1916 station in Elk District, eight miles from Barnum, under F.M. Glenn; the quote is from the state's 4th Biennial Report of the Forest, Game and Fish Warden
evidence.quote: 1916: "This station is located in Elk District, Mineral County, eight miles from Barnum, and is under the supervision of F.M. Glenn.
The elevation is 3,327 feet and commands a view of about 800 square miles.

evidence.supports: Watchman lived five miles away and went home each night
evidence.quote: The watchman, Charles H. Broadwater, lives five miles from the station, and goes home each night.

evidence.supports: Station one story high; cabin planned for the watchman
evidence.quote: The station is only one story high, but a cabin will be built in the near future so that the watchman may remain there overnight in extremely dry weather.

evidence.supports: Seven miles of phone line built to the station; New Creek Line
evidence.quote: Seven miles of phone line have been built to this station, three miles being known as the 'New Creek Line,' and connecting with the Mutual Lines at New Creek.

evidence.supports: 1926 Charleston Gazette item on the Pinnacle Knob tower telephone, served from the New Creek Valley line
evidence.quote: The Pinnacle Knob tower telephone is served from the New Creek Valley line which is connected with the Keyser central office.

evidence.supports: Photo from the rebuilt fire tower, taken in 1964
evidence.quote: A view from the rebuilt fire tower taken in 1964.

evidence.supports: By 2003 only the frame of the fire tower was left
evidence.quote: By 2003, only the frame was left of the fire tower.

evidence.supports: By 2003 a large communication tower stood on the summit
evidence.quote: By 2003, large communication tower stood atop Pinnacle Knob.

evidence.supports: Only the foundation of the fire tower remains
evidence.quote: Only the foundation remains of the fire tower.

evidence.supports: Visitor advises a four-wheel-drive vehicle to reach the summit
evidence.quote: I recommend using a four wheel drive vehicle to reach the summit.

evidence.supports: The last part of South Tower Lane is steep
evidence.quote: The last part of South Tower Lane is very steep.

evidence.supports: Fire tower property fell into disuse after World War II; three communications towers now on the site
evidence.quote: The Pinnacle Knob fire tower property fell into disuse after World War II, but found a second life as a home for three communications towers.

evidence.supports: Foundation now a scenic overlook at an elevation well over 3,000 feet
evidence.quote: The second fire tower foundation now serves as a scenic overlook with an elevation well over 3,000 feet.

evidence.supports: Pinnacle Knob is in the Allegheny Wildlife Management Area
evidence.quote: I photographed the Pinnacle Knob Lookout Tower located in the Allegheny Wildlife Management Area.

evidence.supports: Pinnacle Knob is on the Allegheny Front in Mineral County
evidence.quote: This tower is perched on Pinnacle Knob, a section of the Allegheny Front, in Mineral County.

evidence.supports: Account calls the remains of a second fire tower an overlook near three communication towers
evidence.quote: Nearby, the remains of a second fire tower now serve as a picturesque overlook, close to three communication towers.

corrections.why: Atlas Obscura and Fellinis describe a fire tower with a frame and a foundation. The 1916 station was one story high, so 'ground' fits only that earlier station.

notes_for_editor: Record kind 'ground' conflicts with sources that describe a fire tower; correction proposed. Sources disagree on what stands now: Atlas Obscura and Fellinis say only the foundation remains (overlook), but the January 2024 Abandoned Online account calls a 'Pinnacle Knob Lookout Tower' perched on the summit; check on site or with WV DNR before trusting the 'frame gone' status. Build date unknown: the 1916 report describes an existing station, and search snippets from other tourism sites give 1916 and 1939 for the tower, which I did not read and did not use. The 1976 decommission and 2008 restoration/NHLR listing claimed in a search snippet were not verified; the NHLR cache has no Pinnacle page for West Virginia. Access level 'public' is inferred from the WMA location and visitor accounts, not from an agency page. Atlas Obscura's 1964 photo caption ('rebuilt') is undated as to the rebuild.
